settings.subtitle: Configure how OwnTracks reports locations to Homey. The configuration here needs to match the settings in the OwnTracks app.

comparison.title: Choosing MQTT or HTTP
comparison.mqttPros: Fast, efficient, and well suited to frequent location updates. It supports live updates and can work reliably when the phone changes networks.
comparison.mqttCons: Requires a broker, broker credentials, and extra setup on both Homey and each phone. The broker must be accessible from both Homey and the phones outside the local network.
comparison.httpPros: Simple to set up with a personal endpoint URL created by the app. Athom securely and reliably relays updates from its service to Homey, and no MQTT broker is needed.
comparison.httpCons: HTTP is less suited to very frequent updates than MQTT. Commands can't be pushed to the phone, so Homey has to wait for the phone to connect to send updates.

mqtt.title: Setting up MQTT mode
mqtt.body:
1. Set up an MQTT broker (self-hosted, or a cloud broker such as EMQX Serverless). It must be reachable from both Homey and every phone even when outside the local network.

2. Create a broker account (username/password) - either one shared account for the whole family, or a separate account per person.

3. Here in the app settings, select **MQTT**, then fill in the **Broker URL**, **Port**, **Use TLS**, **Username** and **Password**, and click **Save changes**. The **Username** and **Password** are for the broker account Homey uses to connect. This can be a separate account created for Homey, or one of the broker accounts already used by an OwnTracks user.

4. On each phone, install OwnTracks and set the connection mode to MQTT (Private). Enter the same Host/Port/TLS setting and that phone's broker Username/Password.

5. In Homey, pair a "User" device for each family member (Devices > Add device > Homey Tracks > User).

6. Open each Homey device's Advanced Settings. The **OwnTracks / MQTT username (User ID)** value is case-sensitive and must exactly match the corresponding OwnTracks value, including uppercase and lowercase letters.

Individual MQTT logins
Use that person's broker **Username**. For example, if Adrian's MQTT username is **Adrian**, set his Homey device's **OwnTracks / MQTT username (User ID)** to **Adrian**. Values such as **adrian** or **ADRIAN** will not match.

Shared MQTT login
When every phone uses the same broker Username, use each phone's unique OwnTracks **Device ID** instead. For example, with the shared broker username **family**, set Adrian's OwnTracks Device ID and Homey value to **Adrian**, and Jackie's to **Jackie**, matching the case exactly.

7. Tap the report button in OwnTracks to test - the matching Homey device's capabilities should update within a few seconds.

http.title: Setting up HTTP mode
http.body:
1. Here in the app settings, select **HTTP** and click **Save changes**. No broker is needed for this mode.

2. In Homey, pair a "User" device for each family member (Devices > Add device > Homey Tracks > User).

3. After creating the device, note the personalized HTTP endpoint URL shown (also available afterwards on that device's Advanced Settings page).

4. On each phone, install OwnTracks, set the connection mode to HTTP, and paste that person's endpoint URL as the target.

5. Tap the report button in OwnTracks to test - the matching Homey device's capabilities should update within a few seconds.

zones.introShared: Shared zones are available to everyone.
zones.introUser: Each user can disable shared zones and keep private zones.
zones.helpChevron:
Showing shared zones
In a user section, select the chevron beside **Shared** to show or hide the shared zones. They are hidden by default.
zones.helpMove:
Moving to Shared
Use the up-arrow icon beside a private zone to move it to **Shared**. It is removed from that user's private list, enabled in their shared list, and made available to every paired user. The move is refused if a different shared zone already has the same name.
zones.helpBody:
Zones are called waypoints in OwnTracks. Each zone has a name, centre point and radius. When a user's reported position enters or leaves that radius, Homey updates the user's Zone and Presence capabilities and can trigger the zone Flow cards.

Shared section
Zones created on the **Shared** tab are available to every paired user. Edit or delete them there to change them for everyone. On a user's tab, untick a shared zone to disable it only for that user; the shared zone itself is not deleted.

User sections
Select a user's tab to see that user's enabled shared zones and **Private** zones. Private zones belong only to that user, so editing or deleting one does not affect anyone else. A zone created on a phone is imported as private for that paired user.

Copying private zones
Use the copy icon beside a private zone to give other users independent copies. Later edits are not shared between those copies.

Synchronization
Homey sends each user their enabled shared zones plus their private zones. MQTT updates are pushed to OwnTracks; HTTP updates are returned when OwnTracks contacts Homey. Changes may therefore appear after the next connection or location report.

map.filterHint: Select the users and dates to show on the map.
map.filterHelpBody:
Use the check boxes to choose which users are displayed on the map. Changes are shown immediately.

Select **My Journeys** beside a user to list that user's recorded journeys. From there, choose a journey to display its route on the map.

Use the date shortcuts or **From** and **To** fields below to limit the coordinates and journeys to a date range. Select **Done** when you have finished.
map.journeyHelpBody:
Choose a journey from the table to display it on the map. Use the date range below to limit which journeys are listed.

**Gap (minutes)** controls how recorded points are grouped into journeys. When the time between two consecutive points is longer than this value, a new journey begins. Increase it to join trips separated by longer pauses, or decrease it to split them sooner.

**Copy track points** places the selected journey's points on the clipboard as tab-separated values (**TSV**), ready to paste into a spreadsheet or text editor. The columns are timestamp, local time, latitude, longitude, accuracy in metres, reported speed in km/h, distance from the previous point in metres, and implied speed in km/h.
map.journeyHelpBack: Select X in the top-right corner of the journey list to return to user selection.
map.deleteJourneyConfirm: Delete all points in this journey? This cannot be undone.
map.deletePointConfirm: Delete this track point? This cannot be undone.
